- When sentiment is consistently low or neutral (≤0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to recent mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (≥0.6) but forecast is flat or declining, model underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% per sentiment unit above 0.6.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (alternating 0.4–0.8), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days or use 14-day smoothed trend instead of 30-day.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 30-day moving average), model often holds too high; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per reversion day.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is weak or negative, model tends to overcorrect; apply a 1–2% downward bias to avoid overconfidence in recovery.
